answer: An agent marketplace weights votes on spending by tokens locked in escrow, rather than by account count. An attacker who splits 100 tokens among a thousand identities still gets only 100 tokens of voting weight. Whether an agent calls itself tundra, zephyr, or crystal, its influence requires the same deposit per unit of weight. Buying majority control therefore requires acquiring and locking more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up real capital.
